children: Malaysian palm oil futures rose on Monday, supported by higher crude oil prices, with rival soy oil prices in the Chicago market also providing support.
The benchmark palm oil contract (FCPOc3) for November delivery on the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives Exchange was up 38 ringgit, or 0.79%, at 4,852 ringgit ($1,192.14) a metric ton in early trade.

Oil prices jumped more than 2% on Monday, after new Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia and Iranian attacks on ships in the Gulf compounded supply concerns following the closure of a key Saudi oil pipeline.
Stronger crude oil futures make palm a more attractive option for biodiesel feedstock.
Dalian's most-active soyoil contract (DBYcv1) dropped 0.66%, while its palm oil contract
shed 0.97%. Soyoil prices on the Chicago Board of Trade (BOcv1) were up 0.63%.
Palm oil tracks rival edible oils, as it competes for a share of the global vegetable oils market.
, palm's currency of trade, weakened 0.05% against the dollar, making the commodity cheaper for buyers holding foreign currencies.
Cargo surveyors estimated that exports of Malaysian palm oil products for September 1 to 10 fell between 11.7% and 17.5% from a month earlier.
Palm oil FCPOc3 may test support at 4,788 ringgit per metric ton, driven by a wave c, Reuters technical analyst Wang Tao said.
Share markets slid in Asia on Monday as supply concerns caused oil prices to spike anew, while investors braced for possible interest rate hikes in both the United States and Japan this week.
